answer: Agents in a decentralized economy can resist sybil attacks by tying participation to a unique hardware-bound identity that must first be validated at a designated physical wharf, where biometric and device fingerprints are cross-checked. Only after clearing this gate can an agent begin climbing the contribution-based summit, with voting weight scaling solely by verified long-term value delivered rather than sheer number of accounts, ultimately allowing only authentic participants to reach the zenith of network governance.
